key_idea: Assume the dyadic transfer operator grows too fast (ρ>2), use that growth to build an affine-covariant probability law on normalized conformal maps, and get a contradiction by computing the sign of the expected Jacobian of the critical-point map of y^k/|F−ξ| in two ways: algebraically it is positive from the log-derivative moments, while pairing each saddle with a maximum forces it to be nonpositive.
reason: The core is striking. The weights telescope into a covariant measure, the parameter k is tuned so that the expected Jacobian collapses to k(k−1)>0, and a Morse-type pairing of saddles with maxima forces the opposite sign. That gives a real conceptual reason for the exponent. However, the argument carries a heavy load of measurability, compactness, escape estimates, exceptional-target handling and box-exhaustion bookkeeping, so the line of attack cannot be held in the head and is far from a book proof.
